headline: The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 sets new corporate taxes, drug price rules, Medicare cost limits, and large energy and climate spending programs.
what_it_does: The law adds a 15% minimum tax on very large corporations and a 1% excise tax on certain stock buybacks. It lets Medicare negotiate prices for some high-spending brand-name drugs starting in 2026 and requires drug makers to pay rebates when prices rise faster than inflation. It caps Medicare prescription drug out-of-pocket costs at $2,000 starting in 2025 and limits insulin copays to $35 a month. It also extends and creates many tax credits for clean energy, electric vehicles, and home efficiency, and funds IRS, energy, climate, and agriculture programs.

who_it_affects.group: Large corporations with over $1 billion in average annual financial statement income
who_it_affects.how: They may owe a 15% minimum tax starting in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.

who_it_affects.group: Publicly traded corporations that buy back their own stock
who_it_affects.how: They must pay a 1% excise tax on the value of repurchased stock after 2022, with listed exceptions.

who_it_affects.group: Medicare beneficiaries who take prescription drugs
who_it_affects.how: Their annual out-of-pocket drug spending is capped at $2,000 starting in 2025, and insulin copays are capped at $35 a month.
They must negotiate Medicare prices for selected drugs starting in 2026 and pay rebates on drugs whose prices rise faster than inflation.

who_it_affects.group: People with income up to 150% of the federal poverty line who have Medicare drug coverage
who_it_affects.how: Starting in 2024, they can receive full premium subsidies and a $0 deductible under the low-income subsidy program.

who_it_affects.group: Households buying clean energy, electric vehicles, or home efficiency upgrades
who_it_affects.how: They may claim tax credits for solar, heat pumps, home improvements, and new or used qualifying electric vehicles, subject to income and price limits.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy health insurance on their own
who_it_affects.how: Premium tax credit rules are extended through 2025, including eligibility for taxpayers with income above 400% of the federal poverty line.

who_it_affects.group: Farmers, ranchers, and rural small businesses
who_it_affects.how: They may qualify for USDA conservation, renewable energy, and rural energy assistance programs.

when_it_takes_effect: Effective dates vary by provision, with the corporate minimum tax applying to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, Medicare drug negotiation starting in 2026, and the Medicare out-of-pocket cap starting in 2025.
